title: Workflow Orchestration
interviewAnswer: Orchestrators schedule and coordinate multi-step workflows, track dependencies, retries and failures, and separate workflow control from transformation logic.
why: Workflow orchestration coordinates dependencies, retries, schedules and observability across data/ML tasks.
intuition: A pipeline is a graph of tasks with dependencies. The orchestrator decides when each task runs, retries failures and records status rather than embedding scheduling logic in scripts.
deepDive: Orchestrators manage DAGs, parameters, retries, backfills, scheduling and metadata. Tasks should be idempotent so reruns are safe. Separate orchestration from business transformation code. Event-driven triggers fit some workloads; schedules fit others. Backfills require versioned code/data assumptions to avoid silently mixing old data with new logic.
workedExample: An ADF/Airflow-like flow could extract source tables, run transformations, validate row counts, publish features and then trigger model training only when upstream tasks succeed.
commonMistakes: Putting complex transformations directly into orchestration definitions.
Making tasks non-idempotent so retries duplicate data.
Using time-based dependencies instead of explicit data/task completion signals.
production: Emit run IDs, lineage and task-level metrics; design retries, timeout and alert policies from failure modes rather than using defaults.
